newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's December CPI +0.8 vs +0.6 in November.
newsitem.headline: Israel's December CPI +0.8 vs +0.6 in November.

text.p: The Central Bureau of Statistics issued the following economic indicator on Wednesday:
ISRAEL CONSUMER PRICES Dec 96 Nov 96 Dec 95
Note: To compare previous indices based on 1987=100.0, multiply indices from January 1994 by 2.421.

The bureau said the December consumer price index was lifted by a sharp 1.9 percent increase in housing prices, as well as a big increase in home-maintenance costs. Offsetting that was a two percent decline in fresh produce prices.
The wholesale price index registered an 0.2 percent decline.
The index was at the upper end of expectations.

For full-year 1996, Israeli inflation reached 10.6 percent, up from 8.1 percent in 1995. The sharpest rises were in health costs, which rose 14 percent, and housing prices, which rose 13 percent, the bureau said.
Wholesale prices rose 7.0 percent for the year, down from 10.0 percent for 1995.
The market responded with mild disappointment to the December index. Analysts said it reduced the chances that interest rates would come down at the end of the month as some had hoped.

"The index is a little disappointing. It's at the top end of the range of expectations, but it's not terrible. I was not expecting the Bank of Israel to lower interest rates this month," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
Shahar Gazit of Betucha Securities and Investments also expressed disappointment, saying he was expecting a rise of 0.6 to 0.7 percent.
